prompt: Put the three rungs in order, from the bottom.
"17.3% of first deliveries are late." Which rung is this?
hint: Does it say what to do?

choices.text: An observation: true, checkable and inert
choices.why: It says neither whether it matters nor what to do.
It gives no consequence or cause.
Nobody could act on it on Monday.

prompt: Why do analyses stop on the first rung, by the lesson?

choices.text: Because recommendations belong to managers and analysts should stay neutral

choices.why: Interpretation and recommendation are claims that might be.

prompt: Which are observations wearing a recommendation's clothes? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: We should look into first deliveries
choices.why: Look how, by whom, to decide what?

choices.text: Sandra's team removes the check in the interior from 1 September
choices.why: Action, owner and date: somebody can start on Monday.

prompt: Match each part of Faro's recommendation to its content.

pairs.right: Remove the manual check for confirmed addresses
Interior late share from 23.6% to 8% or less

prompt: "Logistics" is named as owner. What is wrong, by the lesson?
hint: A function is not a person.

choices.why: A department is not an owner.

choices.text: Logistics did not cause the problem in the first place, so it should not own it
choices.why: Ownership of the fix is not blame.

choices.text: A function is an alibi, not an owner
choices.why: A named team with a named lead is an owner.
Finance does not run the warehouse.

prompt: Which part is the commonest omission, by the lesson?

choices.text: The measure used to judge it
choices.why: Often missing, and not the commonest.
A date is what tells the owner this is a priority.

prompt: Besides the five parts, a recommendation carries its reason in one ___.
hint: A short piece of a sentence.

prompt: Why include "do nothing" in the options table?

choices.text: Its cost is the strongest argument for acting
choices.why: About 510 early cancellations a year continue.

choices.text: To make the others look better
choices.why: It is a real option, not furniture.

prompt: Promising three days instead of two would cut late first deliveries on paper. Why does the lesson reject it?

choices.text: It costs more than the express service

choices.why: Moving the goalposts; lesson 12 names the effect.

choices.text: It is illegal under the consumer protection code to change a delivery promise
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so.

prompt: About how many thousand reais a year would the express service cost for every first box?
hint: R$ 9 each, about 12,226 first boxes a year.

prompt: Paulo picks the express service instead of your recommendation. What does the lesson say?

choices.why: That is the error lesson 4 warns about.
The decision was made with costs and risks in view.

prompt: Why is the bottom of Marina's range half the effect?

choices.text: It is a judgement about two untested assumptions
choices.why: Reaching 8%, and late customers behaving like on-time ones once fixed.
It is stated as a judgement, with a reason.

prompt: To the nearest whole customer, how many customers a year does Calc say the change would keep at 8% late?
What is the most useful thing a range can show, by the lesson?

choices.text: Whether the uncertainty matters to the decision
choices.why: Even the bottom clears the cost here, so the decision does not depend on which end is right.

choices.text: Which assumptions the board approved during the quarterly review of the targets

prompt: Why is the pilot run in the interior?

choices.text: It has the highest late share, 23.6%
choices.why: The change has the most to show there.

prompt: What is the pilot's guardrail?

choices.text: Late first deliveries at 8% or less

choices.why: Chosen before the pilot, not after.
That is the lagging check, months later.

prompt: Why not run a randomised experiment, by the lesson?

choices.text: It would take years to produce any result at all

choices.why: So a split by region is what can be run; the recommendation should say what it cannot rule out.
This one has one: the capital.

prompt: What does the pilot's decision rule cover? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Criterion met and guardrail holds: roll out to the capital
Guardrail fails: keep the check where the lookup cannot confirm
Extend the pilot until it succeeds
choices.why: A pilot extended until success is not a test.

prompt: When does the lesson say a test is the right recommendation?

choices.text: Always, because tests are safer than decisions
choices.why: Not always: when the effect is certain, act.
Then try small, time-boxed, with the go result decided first.
